To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the translation of literary works and of titles of plastic art works, is a process that is based on the translator's intervention into the original text.
the translator's intervention is not only oriented towards a minimum semantic equivalence of the text, but also towards the preservation of the original's artistic dimension.
the translation of artistic titles and literary works is a process that is based on three directions: exoticization, domestication and cultural leveling".
In summary, our research is concerned with
the translation of literary works and titles of works of visual art.
the translation of literary works and titles of plastic works of art.
the translator's strategies of domestication and exoticization, as well as the levelling of cultural elements in the process of literary translation and of titles of plastic art works.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the theory of literary translation, as well as the practice of translation in general, are based on the following principles: 1) equivalence; 2) adequacy; 3) adequacy and equivalence.
the translator's intervention is oriented towards three main directions, namely: exotization, domestication and leveling.
, as regards literary translation, it is necessary to take into consideration the cultural specificity of the source text and to make it accessible for the target audience.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

it is about the translator's intervention, in the process of translating a work of literature, in order to make it accessible for the target audience, while at the same time preserving the originality of the source text.
the translation of literary texts and of the titles of plastic works of art is a process of "domestication and exoticisation", which is also an act of cultural levelling, as it is an act of creation.
it aims at a "cultural levellization" of the text in order to facilitate the reader a better understanding, while preserving the "exotic dimension" of the original text.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the process of translating literary works and titles of plastic arts, the translator must take into account the three above-mentioned directions, as these are essential to the success of the work of translating.

the translator should not be afraid of the "exotic" dimension of the original text and should be able to preserve it in the translation, while at the same time being able to bring together, in the target language, those elements of "exoticism" that are specific to the source language.

, in the case of literary translation, the translator's intervention is not limited to a simple replacement of the linguistic and cultural elements, as the theory of translation suggests, but it also involves a "cultural levellisation" of the elements that are intrinsic only to the original text.
